moat_against: Customer concentration and OEM pricing power — a concentrated set of large equipment customers sets the capex cycle
Violent end-market cyclicality — FY2023 OE fell to $178M in the downturn
Atotech capital allocation — ~$1.8B of impairments within a year of the Aug 2022 close; returns below the deal's cost of capital
Leverage — net debt 9.9x normalized OE amplifies the cycle for equity holders
Specialist competition in every niche and OEM insourcing risk; no owned end-demand
moat_for: Design-in / qualification switching costs in RF power, vacuum, plasma and gas-delivery subsystems — swaps risk process yield
Leading positions in niches — at/near #1 share in RF power supplies, strong vacuum and remote-plasma positions
Breadth and cross-sell — vacuum, photonics, motion and chemistry under one roof, tools plus recurring chemistry and services
Recurring chemistry/services mix (former Atotech) with high attach rates on installed chemistry equipment
moat_justification: Core subsystems are designed into fab tools and processes, where re-qualifying a supplier risks yield — real switching costs — and MKS holds leading share in several niches, with recurring chemistry/services on top; but it sells to powerful OEM customers into a violently cyclical end market, and the 2023 impairments on the just-closed Atotech deal (~$1.3B Materials Solutions plus ~$0.5B Equipment Solutions) show parts of the portfolio were worth far less than the price paid, with returns on capital since running below the deal's cost.
name: MKS Inc.
one_liner: Entrenched semi-equipment subsystem supplier, moat 6/10, in a strong AI upcycle — but at $226.70 the weighted IRR is only 5.64% (IV@15% $53.74); it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$54, and even the super-bull case doesn't reach a 10% IRR at this price.
